names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 18 Δεκεμβρίου, «Όσιος Φλώρος επίσκοπος Αμινσού ή Αμισού», with the rank word and the see left off. The page glosses the name itself, «(από το λατινικό flos - floris = άνθος) = ο ωραίος σαν το λουλούδι», and gives the see's name two forms, «Αμινσού ή Αμισού».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s second heading for 18. децембар ст. ст., „Свети Флор, епископ амински.“ — with «Свети» left off, which §5 says is not a rank, and «епископ амински» left off, that being the `bishop` grade §5 maps, `types` keeps and `office` carries. The bare forename is what is left; the heading gives no epithet. THE FOLD WAS MEASURED BEFORE THE FORM WAS WRITTEN AND IT IS A REAL ONE: `fk.mjs` puts the key `флор` at ONE other holder, `florus-of-illyricum`, whose Serbian form came off this same book for the Julian 18 August — so this form takes the fold from one member to two and a new READ_FOLDS key goes into `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in this same commit.

floruit.note: saint.gr dates him by the reigns and the patriarchates: «έζησε την εποχή που βασίλεψαν οι Ιουστίνος Β' (565 - 578 μ.Χ.), Τιβέριος (578 - 582 μ.Χ.) και Μαυρίκιος (582 - 602 μ.Χ.) και επί των πατριαρχών Κωνσταντινουπόλεως Ευτυχίου και Ιωάννου του Γ'». No year of birth and no year of death is given; it says only that he died in deep old age.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Φλώρος επίσκοπος Αμινσού ή Αμισού»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. **The page calls Amisos a city of Cappadocia — «έγινε επίσκοπος Αμισού που είναι πόλη της Καππαδοκίας» — and gives the see two names; no coordinate is proposed.** It names his father Φλώρος and his mother Ευφυΐα, his wife and child whom he saw die, the small estate at the place called Ανάπλουν where he withdrew, and the patriarchs Eutychius and John III; none of them is a folder this reading could attach to and no `related` row is made. It prints no hymn. The corpus keeps a `florus-of-illyricum` on 18 Αυγούστου, the stonemason martyred with Laurus, who is not this bishop.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 31.12.2025 (18. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети Флор, епископ амински.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. The second calendar to keep him, saint.gr being the first and only. `types` UNTOUCHED: `venerable` for the monastery and the ascetic struggle, which this book states — «повуче се у манастир на подвиг» — and `bishop` for the see, which it states too; the `office` already carries it. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND AGREED TO THE YEAR AT BOTH BOUNDS: the folder’s floruit of 565 to 602 came from saint.gr’s reigns, Justin II, Tiberius and Maurice, and this book prints the SAME TWO FIGURES in its own parenthesis — «Живео у време цара Јустина II и Маврикија (565-602)». It names Justin II and Maurice and not the Tiberius between them, which does not move either bound. **ONE DISAGREEMENT, RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED: THE PROVINCE.** This book puts Amisos «у области Кападокијској», in the region of Cappadocia; saint.gr gives the see only its two name forms, «Αμινσού ή Αμισού», and names no province. Nothing was renamed and no `locations` row was made — the folder has never held a coordinate — and the book’s own words are in the life. NO `related` ROW: the entry names no person at all beyond the two emperors, who are no folders this corpus holds under those names. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: that he was OF NOBLE FAMILY AND A NOBLE HIMSELF — «Беше од племића и племић»; that he left the turmoil and vanity of the world and withdrew into a monastery for the ascetic struggle, FOR THE SALVATION OF HIS SOUL, before he was chosen bishop; and that he pleased God both as an ascetic and as a hierarch and passed over peacefully into the Kingdom of God. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
